accepted_claims: There exists an entire F hypercyclic for differentiation such that zF is not hypercyclic.
For every fixed nonconstant complex polynomial p, the set of F in HC(D) for which pF is not in HC(D) is dense in H(C).
The particular F constructed for p=z and eta=1 also has z^m F not in HC(D) for every integer m>=1.
The polynomial multipliers that preserve all of HC(D) are exactly the nonzero constants.
